info.title: File4Base API Engine
info.description: Enterprise-grade REST and Dynamic Relational DDL Database Engine for File4Base. Supports runtime schema migrations, table occurrences, relationships graph, dynamic Find Mode formula parsing, security ACL, and solution archiving. Every endpoint except the health probes, sign-in and the database selector requires a session token: sign in with POST /api/v1/auth/login and send the returned token as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. A session is bound to the database it signed in to.

put.description: Updates a layout's name and definition. A definition without script_triggers keeps the stored ones. Only an owner or an admin may switch on a script trigger here (move a disabled one into on_layout_enter / on_layout_exit, or change the stored list); anyone else gets 403.

get.description: Every script trigger of every layout and layout object, with the problems that keep it from running and their remedy. File4Base runs OnLayoutEnter, OnLayoutExit, OnRecordLoad, OnRecordCommit, OnRecordRevert, OnModeEnter and OnModeExit set on a layout, and OnObjectEnter, OnObjectExit, OnObjectModify, OnObjectValidate and OnObjectSave set on a field, one script per event of a layout or object. Requires admin (owner or admin role).

put.description: Enables or disables the triggers named, all or none, in one transaction; every layout changed gets a new version, so open clients read it again. An OnLayoutEnter or OnLayoutExit trigger moves into its slot when enabled; every other trigger is switched where it is, in the layout's script_triggers list. Enabling a trigger with a problem, or two of the same event on one layout or object, refuses the whole batch. Requires admin (owner or admin role) and an unlocked design.

delete.description: Deletes the record and, in one transaction, what its cascading relationships reach. A cascade that reaches another solution's table (#107) is planned in full first and refused before anything is deleted when the account held there may not delete what it reaches (403) or that solution cannot be reached (424); that solution's records are deleted first, in a transaction of its own.

post.description: Executes a Find query supporting wildcards (*), single characters (@/?), comparisons (>, <, >=, <=), exact (=), strict (==), negation (! / !=), ranges (...), today's date (//), and empty/non-empty search. A criterion on a related field of another solution's table (an external occurrence, #107) is run in that solution as the account the session group holds there; the records searched are then filtered by what they must hold to be related to a match.

post.description: Maps the reference to a solution and resolves the table of each external occurrence through it, reading that solution's catalog with a session of its own (peer_token, owner or admin there). A table is resolved only when tables names it or exactly one table holds every field used; otherwise the occurrence stays unbound with its candidates. Everything is checked first: an unknown occurrence or table in tables answers 422 and writes nothing; otherwise the mapping and the tables are saved together. Reads no record. Requires admin and an unlocked design.

The records it changes are modified, and answered as they are now, so a client updates its found set in place. Needs the edit privilege; at most 10000 records.

field.description: The match field the lookups start from.

200.description: How many records changed, and each of them as it is now

400.description: No looked-up value starts from the field

get.summary: List the SMTP profiles of Send Mail (server administrator, #133)

200.description: profiles, password_env_prefix and the solutions allowed to use the server profile

put.summary: Create or replace the SMTP profile of a solution, or the server-wide one

200.description: The stored profile, without its password

delete.summary: Remove the SMTP profile of a solution (no parameter: the server-wide one)

post.summary: Send one test message through an SMTP profile

put.summary: Allow a solution to send through the server-wide SMTP profile, or withdraw it (off by default, #133)

200.description: The solution and whether it may use the server profile

get.summary: Whether the session's solution can send mail through SMTP (#133)

200.description: smtp_configured, scope, from_name, from_address, max_per_hour, max_recipients, max_attachment, max_batch

post.summary: Send Send Mail messages through the session's SMTP profile (#133)
post.description: 1 to 100 messages sharing sender and attachments; at most 32 MiB per request, 50 recipients and 20 MiB of attachments per message. CR, LF or NUL in an address, the sender name, the subject or an attachment name is refused. A sender of another domain than the profile's becomes the reply-to address. On an SMTP failure, 502 carries sent and filemaker_error (1501-1506).

200.description: sent: how many messages were sent

source_field_id.description: FileMaker id of the field a migrated column comes from, set by the migration and by restoring a solution bundle; absent for a column created here. Another solution's external occurrences find the field by it when their document names it by id only (#107).

calculation_formula.description: Formula expression or summary operation JSON

TableOccurrence.description: A table occurrence: of a base table of this solution (base_table_id), or of another solution's table (external, no base_table_id).

operator.description: Operator of the first match criterion: =, ≠, <, ≤, >, ≥ or × (always matches). <>, !=, <=, >= and x are read as their sign.

allow_creation.description: The right side's "Allow creation of records in this table via this relationship": a record of the left occurrence may create records of the right one through it.

cascade_delete.description: The right side's "Delete related records in this table when a record is deleted in the other table": deleting a record of the left occurrence's table deletes its related records of the right one.

sort_related.description: The right side's "Sort records": the order its records are read in from a record of the left side, as field names of the right table separated by commas, each prefixed with - to sort descending ("asc" and "desc" sort by the match field). An empty string clears it; a portal's own sort wins.

left_allow_creation.description: The left side's allow-creation: a record of the right occurrence may create records of the left one through it.

left_cascade_delete.description: The left side's cascade delete: deleting a record of the right occurrence's table deletes its related records of the left one.

left_sort_related.description: The left side's "Sort records": the order its records are read in from a record of the right side, as for sort_related.

predicates.description: Every match criterion in order; a record is related when it meets all of them. The first is the relationship's own left_column_id, operator and right_column_id. Always returned. On create, replaces the single pair; on update, replaces every criterion, and leaving it out leaves them unchanged. An empty list is refused.

left_column_id.description: A field of the left occurrence's table.

left_column_name.description: The field's name. Required, instead of the id, on a side on an occurrence of another solution's table.

right_column_id.description: A field of the right occurrence's table.

right_column_name.description: The field's name. Required, instead of the id, on a side on an occurrence of another solution's table.

RelationshipPredicate.description: One match criterion. A side on an external occurrence names its field (left_column_name / right_column_name) and has no column id.

linked.description: The solutions the sign-in tried the same credentials in; omitted when the solution reads none.

ProblemDetails.description: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs

user.description: Username of the first owner account

password.description: Password of the first owner account

setup_code.description: Setup code printed in the server log (or FILE4BASE_SETUP_CODE). Only read for a reserved database, by a caller who is not a super-owner. Case, spaces and dashes are ignored.

active.description: Database of the caller's session; empty when signed out

reference.description: The file reference the occurrence goes through.

database.description: The solution the reference is mapped to; empty while unmapped.

reason.description: not_signed_in: sign in to that solution (POST /api/v1/auth/link). no_access: the account held there may not read the table. schema_mismatch: the table or a field is no longer there. missing: the reference is unmapped or unbound, the solution is not installed, or the operation is not done across solutions yet.

ExternalOccurrence.description: What an occurrence of another solution's table holds in place of a base table (#107).

file_reference.description: The file reference, by id or name on create; its name in responses.

database.description: The solution the reference is mapped to; empty while unmapped.

table.description: The table's name in that solution; empty while unbound.

fields.description: Fields used through the occurrence, by name; a field the migrated document names by FileMaker id only is its marker "#<id>".

candidates.description: Tables holding every field used (a marker by source_field_id), when the table is not known. Never chosen automatically.

resolved.description: For each "#<id>" marker, the field of the bound table whose source_field_id it is. The stored marker is kept.

LinkedSolution.description: A solution the session group reads through its external occurrences, and whether it is signed in to it.

references.description: The file references mapped to it.

token.description: Bearer token of the linked session; given only when it is linked.

EvaluationContext.description: The record of the layout a portal's rows are evaluated in, as FileMaker evaluates a portal row's conditions and the portal's filter: from the layout, with the row as the current record of the portal's occurrence. A field named alone, of the portal's occurrence or of one reached through it reads the row; one of the layout's occurrence reads this record, any other is related to it; an aggregate of the portal's occurrence covers every record related to this one. The caller must be able to read its table; the occurrence must be one of this solution's tables.

occurrence.description: The layout's occurrence, by id or name.

side.description: The end of the relationship whose records are wanted, which a relationship joining an occurrence to itself needs for its left end.

sort.description: The order of each record's related records, as ?sort= of the single read: field names, each descending or not. The relationship's own order when omitted.

records.description: The related records of each record asked for, by record id.

RecordPrivileges.description: What the session may do with a table's records. For another solution's table, what the account the session holds there may do (#107).

committed.description: The solutions whose related records are already deleted.

database.description: The solution whose records could not be deleted, and are still there.

ScriptTrigger.description: A script trigger of a layout or of one of its objects (#26). A trigger imported from FileMaker arrives disabled and marked quarantined_by_migration.

object_id.description: The layout object the trigger is set on, when it was migrated.

script_id.description: The script it runs, when it exists in the solution.

can_enable.description: Disabled, and nothing keeps it from running once enabled.

MailProfile.description: An SMTP profile of the Send Mail script step (#133). It never holds its password: password_env names an environment variable of the server, starting with FILE4BASE_SMTP_, that does.

solution.description: The database the profile is for; empty for the server-wide profile.

password_env.description: Name of the server environment variable holding the password; must start with FILE4BASE_SMTP_.

max_per_hour.description: Messages one account may send per hour.

password_available.description: Whether the password variable is set on the server. The password itself is never answered.

bearerAuth.description: Opaque session token returned by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Bound to one user and one database; expires after a period of inactivity (SESSION_TTL, default 12h).

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or expired session token

Forbidden.description: The session's role or layout permissions do not allow this operation

ExternalUnavailable.description: The request reads or writes records through an occurrence of another solution's table, which cannot be reached there: not signed in, no access, schema mismatch, or not done across solutions yet (#107). Never answered from a local table.

PartialDelete.description: A cascading delete deleted related records in another solution, in a transaction of its own, then failed in this one, whose records are still there (#107). Deleting again once the cause is fixed finishes it, but the re-run may leave records reachable only through the committed part.
